source.title: Negative Preference Optimization: From Catastrophic Collapse to Effective Unlearning
source.authors: Rui-Qi Zhang; Li-Cong Lin; Yu Bai; Song Mei

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports unlearning and utility results, but does not test recovery after unlearning by fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting. Its forgetting metrics therefore do not test the claim versions about recovery or resistance to recovery.
record.gate_note: The paper mentions extraction attacks and robust unlearning in related work, but those are citations, not tested results. Its own Forget Quality, utility, and training-trajectory results describe unlearning performance, not whether attacks recover targeted knowledge.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes NPO and evaluates it on TOFU (Llama-2-7B-chat) and a synthetic task using Forget Quality (KS-test p-value vs a retrained model) and Model Utility. It runs no recovery attack (relearning fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization, or prompting/jailbreaks) on any unlearned model. Version A's core, that simple attacks fail to recover knowledge, is therefore not tested. Its forgetting metric is similarity to a retrained model, not accuracy near chance on hazardous knowledge. F is not tested either: NPO is not shown to resist any attack. Related-work mentions of extraction attacks and Lynch et al. are citations only. The authors list adversarial prompts as future work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that NPO avoids GA's catastrophic collapse and achieves state-of-the-art forget/utility trade-offs on TOFU, including the first effective unlearning of 50% or more of the data. They leave harder scenarios such as adversarial prompts to future work.
record.recipe_differences: NPO is a new unlearning objective, not an implementation of the recovery attacks or methods in the claim. It is compared with GA and other unlearning baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the retain-loss weight changes Forget Quality and Model Utility; GA outcomes depend on an instance-specific stopping time. Synthetic-task outcomes and learning-rate choices also vary by setting.

fits_no_version.finding: On TOFU with Llama-2-7B-chat, GA and GA+RT Forget Quality peaks early, then collapses. On Forget05 and Forget10 the peak stays below 0.05. NPO-based methods plateau stably. NPO+RT alone passes the 0.05 threshold on Forget10, and with tuned retain weights it does so on Forget50 and Forget90 with utility above 0.55.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On TOFU, NPO-based unlearning gives a better Forget Quality / Model Utility trade-off and avoids GA's catastrophic collapse. This says nothing about whether the forgotten knowledge is recoverable.

record.problems: TOFU uses fictitious profiles that the text says do not exist in pre-training data. The paper notes that beyond Forget10, Truth Ratio is still evaluated on the standard Forget10 subset as a proxy for the full forget set. No recovery attacks are evaluated.
record.rows_left_out: Other baseline and NPO curves, auxiliary metrics, and synthetic-experiment distances are not included because they measure unlearning/utility comparisons rather than recovery after unlearning.

untested.parts: No attack of any kind is applied after unlearning. Forget Quality measures indistinguishability from a retrained model, not targeted accuracy near chance.
No relearning or fine-tuning after unlearning.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocking versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context probes. Adversarial prompts are named only as future work.
NPO is a new unlearning method, but its robustness to recovery attacks is not evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification and the rows' ['none'] links are correct. All rows are unlearning-quality results, not recovery tests, so cannot_determine is appropriate with respect to the claim versions. R7 and R8 compare the study's own method with baselines; this is acceptable as context but carries no verdict weight. TOFU uses fictitious authors not present in pre-training data.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether any attack recovers knowledge after unlearning; its Forget Quality measure compares the unlearned model with a retrained model rather than measuring accuracy against chance.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning set.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing that unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context recovery test.
NPO is proposed and evaluated for unlearning quality and utility, but it is not tested against the recovery attacks in the claim.
